business_problem: IBM Z hardware teams were coordinating manufacturing, chip design, firmware, operating-system, test and defect-tracking work across several tools, making secure traceability, dependency management and compliance reporting harder than they needed to be.
solution_summary: IBM's zHW platform teams selected IBM Engineering Workflow Management as the central workflow hub for product development after a year-long comparison against multiple alternatives. The objective was to replace several existing tools with one environment capable of supporting secure collaboration, large attachments, long-lived engineering records and complex dependency tracking across chip design, hardware, firmware, operating-system and test activities. IBM Engineering Workflow Management becomes the system of record for work items and their relationships, while IBM Engineering Lifecycle Management and IBM Engineering Test Management provide adjacent lifecycle and testing capabilities. The combined environment supports configurable workflows, role-based access restrictions, auditability and reporting for leaders who need to understand whether upstream deliverables threaten downstream milestones. Rather than forcing teams to conform to disconnected tools, the implementation lets the development process be encoded directly in the workflow platform, improving visibility, governance and traceability for a highly regulated engineering operation.

solution_components.name: IBM Engineering Workflow Management
solution_components.role: Acts as the central hub for engineering work items, dependencies, security controls and reporting across the IBM Z hardware program.

solution_components.name: IBM Engineering Lifecycle Management
solution_components.role: Provides lifecycle-management capabilities that operate in tandem with the workflow hub.

solution_components.name: IBM Engineering Test Management
solution_components.role: Supports the testing threads and associated traceability required in the broader engineering workflow.

data_flow: Engineering work items, test data, dependency relationships and supporting files from IBM Z development streams flow into Engineering Workflow Management, which coordinates lifecycle and test-management integrations and surfaces milestone and risk reporting for stakeholders.
business_outcome: IBM created a more secure, centralized and dependency-aware engineering workflow that is expected to improve milestone visibility, audit readiness and collaboration for large product-development programs on IBM Z.
architecture_clues: The team required support for very large file attachments and years of retained engineering data.
Workflow customization and access restrictions were key selection criteria because of export-control and proprietary-design constraints.
Dependency visibility for upstream and downstream teams was treated as a core reporting requirement.
